rows.judge_notes: The game plays end to end on the server. Each unit is priced in sequence with an 8% spread per side and 2% price impact, so a same-day buy-then-sell always loses coins, and all 37 tests pass (including a random-trade fuzz test). Input validation uses a strict allow-list of fields and goods, and the rules are pure code kept apart from the HTTP layer. The UX is decent: sparklines, quotes, a news log and an end-of-season screen. It is still fairly plain, with no animation or trade feedback beyond the log and a short error message.

The rules in game.mjs are pure and server-side. Each unit is priced at the stock level it leaves behind, with a 6% spread, so same-day round trips lose coins. Inputs are validated, the client cannot set coins, and all 47 tests pass, including randomised no-free-money checks. I read the code and ran `node --test` but did not start the server or play the UI. The UI has price sparklines, quote previews, toasts, a trade-limit indicator, news and an end-of-game overlay. Balance looks harsh (bot median about 32 coins from 100 by the repo's own notes), which is a tuning concern rather than a defect.

The rules are sound. Spread, per-unit price impact, daily caps and server-side validation make an instant buy-then-sell lose money, and the rules in game.mjs are cleanly separated from the HTTP layer. 4 of the 18 tests fail (the same-day round trip, the spread quote, the price clamp and the stall capacity tests), and the UI is a clear card layout with toasts but only basic game feel.
